skill.displayName: Openclaw Complete Backup Delete Fresh Install Restore Cycle

version.changelog: Semver fix follow-up publish and workflow validation update

llm.summary: This skill is meant for OpenClaw backup and recovery, but it includes high-impact delete, install, credential-copying, and global command replacement steps that need careful review before use.

dimensions.detail: Root/sudo access, deletion under ~/.openclaw and /usr/local/bin, pkill usage, and privileged symlink creation are plausible for repair work but overbroad and weakly bounded for a reusable skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill recommends unpinned global npm installs and a direct curl-to-shell installer without version pinning, signature verification, or a separate review step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow is mostly disclosed and user-directed, but broad triggers, copy-paste command blocks, first-match filesystem discovery, and advice to install missing packages based on errors leave important scoping and verification gaps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact creates durable credential-bearing backups, writes bootstrap notes, suggests cron backup entries, and can persistently replace /usr/local/bin/openclaw, all without strong permission, integrity, or rollback controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The backup, restore, reinstall, and cleanup capabilities match the stated disaster-recovery purpose, but the artifact reaches sensitive credentials, OpenClaw state, /root backup paths, npm global installs, and /usr/local/bin command links, so the operational authority is high-impact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only on an isolated or well-backed-up OpenClaw host, avoid the curl-to-shell fallback, pin and verify packages, encrypt or tightly restrict credential backups, replace destructive deletes with reversible moves, and confirm every global binary or symlink target before changing /usr/local/bin.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The destructive and secret-handling nature is visible in the body, but the skill does not provide a strong upfront confirmation and safety checklist before backup/delete/reinstall commands.
[SC2] unexpected: Installing OpenClaw is purpose-related, but piping a mutable remote installer directly to sh is not proportionate without pinning or integrity verification.
[TM1] unexpected: Resetting OpenClaw state is purpose-related, but rm -rf ~/.openclaw occurs before a robust backup integrity and sandbox-restore gate.
[TM2] unexpected: The chained deletion and retention commands are operational shortcuts, but they reduce reviewability and can delete the wrong binary or backup files.
[RA2] expected: Most persistence signals are backup artifacts, bootstrap notes, or cron examples aligned with disaster recovery, but credential-bearing backups and persistent command replacement still require explicit user control.
[PE2] expected: Some elevated access is plausible for global install and service repair, but the artifact uses it across broad filesystem changes and global command linking.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The safety-first framing is only partly supported; the body includes destructive and supply-chain-sensitive steps that deserve stronger warnings.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger text is informal and broad enough to activate for general troubleshooting rather than only deliberate OpenClaw disaster-recovery work.
[T03] unexpected: The static scan's remote-execution concern is supported by the artifact's curl -fsSL https://cli.openclaw.ai/install.sh | sh instruction.
[T09] unexpected: The static scan's plaintext secret-copying and broad deletion concerns are supported by backup commands that copy credentials into /root/BACKUPS and cleanup commands that delete by wildcard.
[T07] unexpected: The static scan's tool-replacement concern is supported by sudo ln -sf /usr/local/bin/openclaw from files selected by broad find commands.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned npm install findings are supported, including global installs and guidance to install whatever dependency an error reports.
